$comment: WHAT THE WINDOW HALF OF THIS PRODUCT IS ALLOWED TO SHIP.
config/payload-boundary.json does this for the engine payload, and its guard fails the
build on a file classified NOWHERE AT ALL. The window half had no equivalent, so the
rule there was the opposite one: package.json build.files says "dist/**", vite copies
public/** into dist/ verbatim, and anything a person dropped into public/ shipped
because nobody had said it should not.
That is how the operator's own purchase list -- internal repo paths, internal request
ids, his second-person deliberations, a written admission that the installer is
unsigned -- ended up in every installer, one click back from home on a stranger's
fresh install. Reproduced on the packaged build, read off the window, before the
change that added this file.
So: every authored file under public/ is classified here, and tools/check-renderer-
payload.mjs fails when one is not. An unclassified file is not assumed innocent.
"operator" means THE PERSON RUNNING THIS COPY WROTE IT, and it is theirs. It is not a
product asset and it must never be in public/, in dist/, or in app.asar. The product
reads it at runtime from the install's own data directory instead (shell/main.cjs),
which is why removing it from the payload does not remove the feature: the operator
keeps the screen and their list, and everybody else does not receive a copy of it.
ADDING A FILE TO "shipped" IS A DECISION ABOUT STRANGERS. The question to answer
before you do it is not "is this file useful" but "would I hand this to someone I have
never met". If the answer needs a paragraph, it is operator data.
Product assets. These go out with the installer and are seen by everyone.
The data/*.json files here are empty projection envelopes -- {"ok": false,
"data": null} shapes that tell a fresh install it is not connected to anything yet.
They carry no readings, and that is what makes them shippable.
data/subscription-catalog.json USED TO BE LISTED HERE, argued for on the grounds that
it was the product's own public pricing and so passed the note's test. The argument was
about privacy and it answered the wrong question. See "withheld" below.
$commentPreview: preview/* is the website's embedded product simulation (R1268 lane W1). It is a
product asset in the strictest sense: it is the page a stranger is shown BEFORE
they have anything of ours, and every value in it is generated in their browser
from a fixed seed in preview/sim-data.js. There is no reading, no hostname, no
address, no account and no path from any real fleet in it -- which is the whole
reason it can be handed to someone we have never met.
It also ships INSIDE the installer, because vite copies public/ into dist/ and
build.files packs dist/. That is deliberate and harmless: it is nine static
files a person can open from their own install, it reaches no network (see the
fails the build if that ever stops being true.
BEFORE ADDING A FILE HERE, the question from the note above still applies: would
you hand this to someone you have never met. For the preview there is a second
one -- can it be generated from the seed. If it has to be measured from a real
machine to be interesting, it does not belong in a preview.

$comment: The operator's own documents. Never in the payload, at any layer.
data/purchase-catalog.json is the shopping list for launching this product: what to
buy, what breaks without it, and why the person running this copy wanted it. The
authored copy lives in private/purchase-catalog.owner.json, which /private/ keeps out
of git; the running copy lives at <userData>/purchase-catalog.json, which the shell
serves to the app window and to nothing else.
The schema stays in "shipped" on purpose. A schema describes a shape and names no
vendor, price, deliberation or path -- it is the product's, and the window needs it
for the same reason the build did.
PRODUCT ASSETS THIS RELEASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SHIP. Not operator data -- nobody's
private document -- but a product surface the owner has ruled out of the launch. Same
enforcement as "operator": never under public/, never in dist/, never in app.asar.
data/subscription-catalog.json is the subscription page's plan catalog, generated by
tools/gen-subscription-catalog.mjs from the engine's entitlement model. It shipped
because public/ ships by default, and #/subscribe and #/pricing rendered it: plan
names, monthly and annual prices, a Team price and a three-seat minimum, generated
2026-08-12. The owner never authorised that catalog (R1214) and his release rule is
"we are NOT collecting payments at first public launch". Nothing could be charged --
there is no live provider and no link to the routes -- but a price a stranger is shown
is an advertisement whether or not a card can follow it.
WHY WITHHELD AND NOT ONE OF THE OTHER THREE ANSWERS. Removing the routes leaves the
bytes in the installer and turns two typed addresses into a silent jump home, which is
the dead door src/route-parse.js exists to refuse. Emptying the file is undone by the
next person who runs the generator -- and tools/check-subscription-claims.mjs would
tell them to. A flag that is off is a flag that can be turned on, and this product
already reads billing configuration out of the environment. The bytes not being there
is the only one of the four that a packaged build cannot undo by itself.
WHAT WOULD HAVE TO HAPPEN FOR A PRICE TO APPEAR AGAIN: this path moves back to
"shipped" in this file, AND a catalog is authored under public/data/ again. Neither
an environment variable, a setting, a stored preference nor a build flag can do it,
and tools/check-renderer-payload.mjs fails the build if the second happens without
the first. The generated catalog itself still lives at config/subscription-catalog.json,
out of the payload, where the claims guard reads it.
data/schema/subscription-catalog.schema.json stays in "shipped" for the reason the
purchase-list schema does: a schema describes a shape and names no price.
